newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says one major bank merger acceptable.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says one major bank merger acceptable.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said a reduction in the number of major Australian banks from four to three would not greatly affect industry concentration or competition.

"However, commentators suggest that the market dynamics in Australia are such that there would quickly be pressures to move from three to two," the central bank said in its submission to the Wallis Inquiry into the nation's financial system.
"If this were to occur, it would give Australia the most concentrated banking industry in the industrialised world and would take us into uncharted prudential waters," it said.

"How could a merger be arranged if one of the two banks got into difficulty? This is a very big step to take and would require community support, but it should not be ruled out of order altogether," the RBA said.

The Wallis Inquiry, which will hand its report to the government by March next year, will consider a range of deregulation issues including the easing of merger restrictions among the four major banks and the two largest life offices.
The RBA said this merger policy, called the "six pillars" should be re-assessed but drew the line at permitting a spate of mergers which left the nation with only two major banks.
The government has warned the banks from launching any mergers during the life of the Wallis inquiry, named after its chairman Stan Wallis, the former head of manufacturer Amcor Ltd.

Analysts believe, however, that mergers will resume soon after with National Australia Bank Ltd tipped to bid for either fellow Melbourne-based major Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd or Sydney-based Westpac Banking Corp.
The other major bank, Commomwealth Bank of Australia CBA.A, is also regarded as a potential predator.
